title: 1st Annual Roger Murray Lecture Series: A Conversation Between Bruce Greenwald and Tano Santos
description: A conversation with Bruce Greenwald, Robert Heilbrunn Professor Emeritus of Asset Management, and Tano Santos, David L. and M. Elsie Dodd Professor of Finance and faculty director of the Heilbrunn Center.
summary: The talk argues that sustainable value comes from companies with durable competitive advantages, such as local monopolies or specialized expertise, rather than those that attempt to diversify into unrelated areas. It contrasts modern specialized firms with legacy 'generalist' companies that lost their protected monopoly status due to globalization, resulting in diminished returns on capital. The speaker specifically advises caution on companies like Amazon and Intel that are wasting capital on poor reinvestments, while highlighting the risks of overpaying for even strong local monopolies like Deere.
